message: No detected input validation: The code reads the CSV with pd.read_csv and drops/replaces NaN values, but performs no schema checks, dtype assertions, or value-range guards on the incoming data.
No detected untrusted source handling: The dataset is loaded from a local file path provided via CLI argument with no checksum verification, authentication, or integrity checks of any kind.

No detected label flipping detection: There is no validation of label values against an expected set, no label distribution comparison, and no use of tools like Cleanlab to detect label noise or flipping.

No detected data poisoning defenses: While CountOutLiers() computes and prints outlier statistics, it only reports them without taking any action to filter or remove suspicious samples, so no actual defense against data poisoning is implemented.

No detected model integrity verification: The code accepts a weights file path via --weights_file argument and passes it to dataset_dl_prediction without any hash check, signature verification, or pinned revision validation before loading.
No detected label distribution validation: The code only checks for NaN counts and outlier percentages but never validates label distribution, class balance, or expected label ranges before training.
No detected backdoor or trigger detection: There is no activation analysis, gradient anomaly detection, or any trigger-detection mechanism in the training loop.
No detected differential privacy: The code uses standard PyTorch optimizers (Adam, RMSprop, SGD) with no differential privacy library (e.g., Opacus) or DP-SGD noise injection.
No detected adversarial robustness testing: There is no use of adversarial testing libraries (Foolbox, ART, etc.) or any FGSM/PGD attack generation anywhere in the code.

No detected metric tampering protection: While a train/test split appears to be performed via `preprocess()`, there is no evidence of a held-out test set isolated from hyperparameter tuning, signed/hashed evaluation data, or multiple independent metric reporters to guard against metric manipulation.
No detected input sanitization: The code reads a CSV and drops NaN rows but performs no shape/range/type validation on input features before passing them to the model.

No detected output bounds checks: Model outputs are collected and rounded for display but there are no NaN guards, sanity-bound checks, or threshold validations applied to predictions before reporting.
No detected prompt injection defenses: This is a numerical regression model (RMR predictor), not an LLM, so prompt-injection defenses are not applicable and none are implemented.
